Standing quietly on one of the busiest streets near London King’s Cross, a stylish restaurant captures the attention of passersby with its aesthetically pleasing interior and long waiting lines. [[1]] Originally a small eatery in Soho, BAO now has seven locations across London, delighting locals with its mouth-watering Taiwanese flavors and unique brand design.
BAO’s journey began with its three co-founders, Erchen Cheng, Shing Tat Chung, and Wai Ting Chung, who met at London’s Slade School of Fine Art. During a trip to Erchen’s hometown in Taiwan, they became fascinated by the charm of Taiwanese street food, which sparked the idea for BAO. [[2]] After much trial and error, they finally developed BAO’s signature bun by combining different traditional techniques. The bun is renowned for its incredibly fluffy texture and variety of fillings, from classic braised pork belly and fried chicken to sweet treats like fried ice cream.
While the food is key to BAO’s success, it is the branding and philosophy that set it apart. As Erchen Cheng once said in an interview, “BAO is more than a place to eat. When you’re sitting in one of our restaurants, you’re sitting in a story—a story that has been designed.” Drawing on her fine arts background, Erchen infused creativity and understanding of Taiwanese culture into BAO’s dining experience. The restaurant is instantly recognizable by its logo, “The Lonely Man,” a figure who regains energy after taking a bite of bao. [[3]] Featuring thoughtful use of color and furniture, BAO’s seven restaurants each reflect aspects of Taiwanese life in their own unique ways.
[[4]] By blending traditional Taiwanese flavors with innovative design, it has introduced Gua Bao to London in a fresh way. As BAO continues to grow, it leaves a lasting impact on both the food scene and cultural appreciation.

options_bank.A: In addition to its strong brand identity, BAO is also known for its trendy interior design.
options_bank.B: This is BAO, a restaurant serving Taiwanese street food, “Gua Bao”—steamed buns filled with braised pork.
options_bank.C: BAO also offers a traditional Karaoke experience for partygoers and music lovers in two of its locations.
options_bank.D: Despite having no formal culinary training, they were determined to craft the perfect bun recipe.
options_bank.E: BAO’s success is a testament to the power of passion, creativity, and cultural storytelling.

tags.topic: BAO, a London restaurant bringing Taiwanese gua bao and design to London
